A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CausalMM and contain readable main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained content can be matched across the appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, attention and layer ablations, GPT-4o evaluations, and qualitative cases in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds model and baseline evaluations in Tables 4–6 and a qualitative failure case in Figure 23.

M1.justification: The attention interventions, vision-only/language-only/multimodal variants, and decoding equations remain unchanged. Applying existing variants to additional backbones and clarifying their description does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The benchmark coverage remains VLind-Bench, POPE on MSCOCO/A-OKVQA/GQA, MME, and LLaVA-Bench. Added POPE evaluations reuse the existing datasets and question settings; the additional qualitative case extends analysis within visual question answering.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds evaluated DoLa and AGLA comparators alongside Regular, VCD and OPERA. This substantially broadens the decoding-method comparison for LLaVA-1.5 and the newly evaluated InstructBLIP configuration.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 substantially expands tested model configurations to Q-former-based InstructBLIP and embedding-autoregressive Chameleon. Chameleon uses the existing language-only variant, while InstructBLIP tests all three variants. Table 6 additionally reports averages across the three POPE datasets; original task settings and metrics remain.

E4.justification: Figure 23 adds a failure case probing humor and high-level semantic understanding. The attention-type and intervention-layer ablations, attention visualizations, and previously reported positive and negative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Table 1 parentheses denote differences from Regular rather than uncertainty; the added tables likewise report point estimates.

E6.justification: Original quantitative results remain unchanged, but Tables 4–6 add substantial results. For example, Chameleon MSCOCO-random accuracy is 61.90 for Regular versus 69.23 for language-only CausalMM. The expanded comparison also shows AGLA exceeding multimodal CausalMM on LLaVA-1.5 adversarial average accuracy, 81.13 versus 80.36; the additions do not establish uniform superiority.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 states adjustment-set conditions and derives the standard back-door formula for a simplified attention–prior–output graph. This formalizes a principle already invoked in v1 without introducing a method-specific identification theorem. Figure 2 also corrects prior-to-visual-attention intervention edges to truncated paths.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the causal-attention framework, hallucination-mitigation and plug-and-play claims. The headline improvements, including 65.3% on VLind-Bench indicators and 164 MME points, are unchanged; additional evaluations support existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 newly explains that reducing prior-induced hallucinations does not necessarily improve high-level semantic understanding, attributing the limitation to the vision encoder and LLM backbone. v1 includes an unsolved refrigerator example but lacks this explicit applicability limitation and explanation.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly states that all cases use direct sampling and explains gamma and the softmax summation index. These are documentation additions, without evidence of rerunning existing experiments. The code-access information and GPT evaluation template remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on causal inference, modality priors and hallucination mitigation, plus sources for newly evaluated models and DoLa. It also explicitly credits Rao et al. for counterfactual attention choices. The related-work organization and central positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely intact, with localized explanations, wording corrections, updated publication/author details and acknowledgments. New appendix sections precede the retained visualization, case-study and evaluation-template sections, which become A.3–A.5.

P2.justification: v2 adds three substantial comparison tables and Figure 23, expanding the displayed experimental evidence. Figures 1–2 are redrawn, including explicit attention-difference graphics and revised intervention arrows. Existing result plots, tables and appendix visualization panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The added architecture and baseline evaluations strengthen support for portability, while the explicit semantic-understanding limitation improves the paper's qualification of its claims. The gain is limited by a generic causal derivation, sparse reproducibility and uncertainty information, and inconsistent new aggregates: Table 6 reports LLaVA-1.5 adversarial OPERA F1 as 79.46, whereas the retained Table 1 entries average 81.74.
